outcomeNote: Single amoraic qualification of the mishna

segments.he: אֵין כְּלִי הַלַּח מְקַדֵּשׁ [וְכוּ׳]. אָמַר רַב, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַסִּי: אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין לִיקְרַב, אֲבָל מְקַדְּשִׁין לִיפָּסֵל.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «the» service «vessels» used for «liquids do not sanctify» dry items. With regard to this halakha, «Rav says, and some say» that «Rav Asi» says: The service vessels used for liquids «do not sanctify» dry items to permit them «for sacrifice» upon the altar, «but they sanctify» dry items in order for the items «to be disqualified» by them, i.e., dry items placed in such vessels may be disqualified by that which disqualifies only sanctified items, e.g., if they are touched by one who immersed that day, or if they emerged from the Temple courtyard.

moves.about: lemma: liquid vessels do not sanctify dry items

moves.summary: not sanctified to be offered, but sanctified to be disqualified

edges.about: lemma: liquid vessels do not sanctify dry items

edges.cueHe: אמר רב ... אין מקדשין ליקרב, אבל מקדשין ליפסל
edges.about: the mishna's 'do not sanctify' means not for sacrifice, though they sanctify to become disqualified
the same dictum is alternatively attributed to Rav Asi

positions.claim: vessels of the wrong kind do not sanctify for sacrifice but do sanctify for disqualification

principlesInvoked: אין מקדשין ליקרב אבל מקדשין ליפסל
